hints: The Fibonacci recurrence is F(n)=F(n-1)+F(n-2), but n is too large for a linear loop.
Use the identity for doubling: F(2k)=F(k)*(2F(k+1)-F(k)).
Recursively compute the pair (F(k),F(k+1)) and derive the pair for n's parity.
analogy: Compute Fibonacci numbers by doubling the index, reusing a pair of neighboring values.
correctness: The doubling identities follow from the Fibonacci recurrence and produce the exact neighboring pair, so recursion on half the index is valid.
complexity: O(log n) time and O(log n) recursion space, or O(1) iterative space.
algorithm: Use fast doubling with the pair (F(k),F(k+1)): c=a*(2b-a), d=a^2+b^2 modulo 1,000,000,007. Recurse on floor(n/2); for even n return (c,d), for odd return (d,c+d).
